public_rationale: Marcus predicts an almost-certain societal outcome, without defining its scale or deadline. Documented AI-generated falsehoods are relevant context, but their occurrence cannot establish that this outcome was almost certain in December 2022. Likewise, its absence by October 2026 would not disprove an undated probabilistic claim. Scoring website growth as support would replace his statement with a weaker claim. The complete statement therefore cannot receive a fair binary assessment under these rules.
limitations: This decision does not establish that the warning was mistaken or that AI misinformation is insignificant.
The persistence of LLMs and the occurrence of AI-generated misinformation do not independently settle the complete claim.
The evidence search provides context; it is not a comprehensive measurement of global misinformation exposure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are here to stay and society is almost certain to be overrun by a tidal wave of misinformation.

statement.excerpt: Like it or not, these models are here to stay, and we as a society are almost certain to be overrun by a tidal wave of misinformation.

from_speaker: these models are here to stay
overrun by a tidal wave of misinformation
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that LLMs will persist and will very probably produce an overwhelming, society-wide influx of misinformation.
“Almost certain” expresses a probability judgment. It must not be replaced with a categorical prediction that misinformation will increase.
The statement supplies no deadline, measurable definition of society being overrun, or framework for assessing its probability judgment.
Counts of AI-generated misinformation sites can document proliferation, but cannot alone establish society-wide exposure or validate the probability assigned in December 2022.
criteria.support_condition: No faithful binary support condition is available for the complete statement as written. Even an overwhelming influx occurring would not by itself establish that it was almost certain when predicted.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No faithful binary contradiction condition is available. Limited misinformation at a later observation date would neither close the unstated horizon nor by itself disprove the probability judgment.
